sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France has a broad network of bilateral investment treaties; applicability depends on the investor's nationality, treaty status, and investment structure. Confirm current entry into force and termination status in the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs treaty database.

France has income tax treaties with numerous jurisdictions, including the United States, the United Kingdom, China, and Canada; verify the treaty and protocol applicable to the relevant residence and income.
EU trade and investment arrangements may apply according to their scope; France is subject to the EU common commercial policy.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French AML/CFT duties are principally governed by the Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), including Articles L.561-2, L.561-2-2, L.561-5, L.561-10, and L.561-15 et seq., and implementing provisions in Articles R.561-1 et seq. SARL beneficial-owner filing is governed by Article L.561-46 of that Code and the Commercial Code provisions governing the National Register of Companies (Registre national des entreprises, RNE), including Articles L.123-36 et seq. and implementing regulations. EU AML requirements, including Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended, also apply.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity document of each foreign individual beneficial owner and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent identity-document authority in the country of issuance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille where the issuing country and France are parties to the Hague Apostille Convention; otherwise consular legalization, unless an applicable treaty waives authentication

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, current company extract, and constitutional documents of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company or commercial registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille where available; otherwise consular legalization, subject to applicable treaty or EU-document exemptions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution or power of attorney authorizing the French incorporation and signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate shareholder, executed by its authorized representative and notarized where required by the place of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille where available; otherwise consular legalization, subject to applicable treaty exemptions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of address and ownership-and-control chart identifying natural-person beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relevant utility, public authority, corporate records, or duly authorized declarant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or consular legalization only where required by the receiving institution or the document's legal form; certified French translation may be required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Apply risk-based customer and beneficial-owner identification, verification, and ongoing monitoring under the Monetary and Financial Code. Screen relevant parties against EU and French asset-freeze lists and United Nations Security Council lists; OFAC screening is not a general French statutory requirement but may be required by US nexus, bank policy, or payment-provider terms. Identify domestic and foreign PEPs, family members, and close associates; apply enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval where legally required. Preserve screening evidence and assess alerts before onboarding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (formalities filing); the INPI Data INPI database is used for company-name and trademark searches. The resulting company information is recorded in the Registre national des entreprises (RNE).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A SARL name may generally use French or other permitted characters and must be distinguishable and lawful. The legal form or its abbreviation, SARL, must appear in company documents and specified public materials. Names must not mislead, infringe earlier company names, trademarks, or other protected rights, or improperly use regulated or protected terms. No general statutory requirement mandates a French-script transliteration.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms implying a regulated activity or professional status without the required authorization
Protected public-authority, state, or public-institution designations used without authorization
Terms protected by third-party trademarks, company names, or other intellectual-property rights
Misleading terms or designations contrary to public order
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France has no general statutory company-name reservation period or standard 30-day reservation. Conduct INPI and trademark searches before filing. If registration formalities are rejected, obtain the reasoned decision, correct the filing or submit supporting evidence through the Guichet unique, and follow the review or appeal route and deadline stated in the decision. A dispute concerning an earlier trade name or trademark may require separate proceedings before the competent court; a rejected filing does not itself establish exclusive name rights.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A SARL must declare a French registered office. A compliant domiciliation provider may be used under the Commercial Code, including Articles L.123-11 et seq., subject to a written domiciliation agreement and provider requirements. A virtual address alone does not establish operational substance, satisfy bank or payment-provider verification, or displace consumer, tax, employment, or regulatory obligations. Home domiciliation may be available subject to statutory conditions, lease terms, co-ownership rules, and local restrictions.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No reliable official percentage is published for unannounced inspections. The risk is not quantifiable as a percentage; inspections or document requests may arise from tax, labor, consumer-protection, customs, AML, or registry authorities based on legal powers and risk indicators.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SARL registration filing and beneficial-owner filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI Guichet unique and applicable registry or filing authorities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Indicative conversion of statutory filing charges; confirm current euro tariff and any applicable filing components at submission.
Regulated annual French tariff for the relevant department and legal form; estimate converted from euros and subject to publication charges.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: French certified translations of foreign corporate and identity documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; varies by language, length, and urgency.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of foreign documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authority in the country of origin and, where applicable, French consular authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Country-specific statutory fees and service charges; estimate only. Authentication may be waived by treaty or EU rules.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French avocat, notaire, or corporate-services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; not a statutory tariff for ordinary SARL incorporation.
Prevailing market benchmark; varies by city, service scope, and contract duration.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name, trademark, and UBO due-diligence screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI databases and private legal or compliance service providers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official database searches may be free or fee-based depending on service; professional screening estimate is a market benchmark.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French bank, notary, or authorized payment institution
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Provider-dependent account, certificate, and administration charges; share capital itself is excluded and no statutory minimum capital applies.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL provisions); Decree No. 2007-431 on commercial registries
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) within the jurisdiction of the registered office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) and Formulaire M0 (Registration Form)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital; however, at least 20% of cash contributions must be paid up at incorporation, with the balance due within 5 years. Capital may be as low as €1, but must be fully subscribed and deposited in a blocked bank account until registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the shareholders hereby subscribe to the share capital of the company as set forth in the Articles of Association, and that the initial contributions be deposited with the designated bank. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office be established at [address] and that the manager(s) named in the Articles be appointed as legal representatives with full powers to act on behalf of the company. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the manager(s) are authorized to complete all registration formalities, including publication of legal notices and filing with the Commercial Court Registry, and to open bank accounts and sign all necessary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (optional but recommended) or private deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Statuts (Articles of Association) in French, including company name, registered office address, corporate purpose (subscription box retail), share capital, share classes, management structure, and governance rules. All shareholders must sign the document. If capital is contributed in cash, deposit funds in a blocked bank account and obtain a certificate of deposit from the bank.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of shareholders and managers
Proof of registered office address (e.g., lease agreement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects the Articles due to missing information, correct the deficiencies and resubmit. Notarization may be required if real estate is contributed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish Legal Notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized legal gazette (JAL) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a notice of incorporation in a JAL, including company name, legal form (SARL), capital amount, registered office, corporate purpose, and duration. The notice must appear before filing with the registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL notice contains errors, publish a corrective notice and obtain a new attestation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Registration Dossier with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) of the registered office's jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Formulaire M0, the Statuts, the JAL publication attestation, the bank deposit certificate, and other required documents to the registry. Pay the filing fee. The registry will issue a K-bis extract upon successful registration.
required_dossiers: Proof of address of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query (e.g., missing document), respond within 15 days with the requested corrections. If the application is rejected, rectify and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain K-bis Extract and Post-Registration Identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and INSEE (National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, the registry issues the K-bis extract (official proof of existence). The company automatically receives its SIREN number and SIRET number from INSEE. These are required for tax, social security, and banking purposes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIREN/SIRET numbers are not received within 10 days, contact INSEE directly to request issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with Tax and Social Security Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) and URSSAF
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company must register for corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés), value-added tax (TVA), and employer social security contributions. This is often done automatically via the registration process, but confirm with the local tax office. Obtain a TVA number if applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or social security registration is delayed, contact the relevant authority with the K-bis extract to expedite.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industrial license required for subscription box retail operations
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No specific operating license required; general business registration (K-bis) suffices

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique (Ministry of Ecological Transition) – Regional Directorate for Environment, Planning and Housing (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – retail and warehousing activities are not listed in the French EIA annexes (Annexe à l'article R.122-2 of the Environmental Code) unless exceeding certain thresholds (e.g., warehouse floor area > 20,000 m²)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with general waste management regulations (Code de l'environnement, Articles R.541-1 et seq.) for packaging waste; adherence to the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) scheme for packaging (Citeo) and electronic waste if applicable. No specific discharge thresholds for wastewater or VOCs for this activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for commercial premises (Code du travail, Articles R.4216-1 et seq.) – obtain a fire safety certificate from the local fire department (SDIS) for premises open to the public or with high occupancy. Structural load inspections for warehouse areas per building codes. Occupational health and safety clearance from the regional health insurance fund (CARSAT) for workplace compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) and official portal impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French SARL obtains SIREN/SIRET from INSEE; non-resident owners appoint tax representative; register for VAT on DGFiP portal with incorporation documents, bank details and financial statements to receive VAT identification number FR followed by SIREN
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections; hybrid mismatch rules and CFC provisions under ATAD apply; specific regimes available for export activities and R&D tax credits

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 85,000 EUR annual turnover threshold triggering mandatory VAT registration
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing for B2B transactions since 1 October 2024 via PEPITES platform with digital timestamps and real-time fiscal clearance

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to physical goods exported outside the EU or to free zones; eligibility requires proof goods have left French territory
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims result in full VAT due plus penalties up to 80% of evaded amount, interest and potential criminal prosecution with retrospective clawback

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France; foreign-exchange policy is principally governed by the European Union and euro-area framework, including the European Central Bank, with French anti-money-laundering supervision involving the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution and the financial intelligence unit TRACFIN.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro, which is fully convertible for ordinary current-account and capital-account transactions. There are no general French exchange controls, restrictions on repatriation of lawful profits, or mandatory use of domestic currency for ordinary commercial payments. Dividend, interest, royalty, and intercompany-payment remittances remain subject to corporate approvals, available distributable profits, withholding-tax analysis, transfer-pricing support, beneficial-owner verification, sanctions screening, and applicable EU and French anti-abuse rules. Cross-border cash movements and certain transactions may trigger statistical, tax, customs, or anti-money-laundering reporting. French resident entities must retain accounting, invoice, contractual, and payment evidence supporting cross-border flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no general deadline requiring export receipts to be converted into euros or deposited with a French bank. Export proceeds may be retained in foreign-currency accounts or received through foreign banks, subject to accounting, tax, customs, sanctions, anti-money-laundering, and payment-services requirements. Exporters must maintain evidence supporting the commercial basis, value, counterparties, and settlement of transactions. Cash and equivalent cross-border movements are subject to applicable EU and French declaration rules, including declaration requirements for physical cash of EUR 10,000 or more when entering or leaving the European Union.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; capital-deposit account or blocked capital account may be arranged for formation or capital increase
Operational Account; capital-deposit account or blocked capital account may be arranged for formation or capital increase

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank / relevant Crédit Agricole regional bank
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; capital-deposit account may be arranged subject to the selected regional entity and formation documentation

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE group bank, including Banque Populaire or Caisse d'Epargne entity
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; capital-deposit account may be arranged subject to the selected group entity
Operational Account; capital-deposit account may be arranged for qualifying French company formations

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for operational collections and payments, but not a complete substitute for a French bank account. A licensed European Economic Area electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide euro payment accounts, SEPA transfers, card acquiring, and subscription-payment functionality under its licence and passporting or local authorisation framework. It may not provide bank deposits or credit unless separately authorised, and safeguarding is not equivalent to deposit-guarantee protection. Provider risk appetite may restrict newly incorporated entities, non-resident owners, high refund volumes, marketplace-like activity, rapid cross-border flows, or physical-goods delivery risks. Offshore digital EMIs outside the European Economic Area cannot lawfully provide regulated payment services to French customers without an applicable EU authorisation, passport, establishment, or other lawful basis. Stripe Billing and comparable processors should be connected to a verified French or EEA business account and supported by clear terms, refund, chargeback, consumer-protection, and transaction-monitoring procedures.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors appear physically to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be permitted after qualified electronic identification, documentary verification, video identification, beneficial-owner verification, and risk-based approval. Individual banks may require an in-person meeting, certified copies, French-resident contact arrangements, proof of operating substance, or an interview with the managing director and ultimate beneficial owners. A SARL formed through a capital-deposit process normally requires evidence of incorporation status, identity and authority of the legal representative, and source of capital before the blocked account or operational account is activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or multi-layered ownership, nominee arrangements, or inability to identify the ultimate beneficial owner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Kbis extract or equivalent registration evidence; articles of association; ownership chart to each natural-person beneficial owner; passports or national identity documents; proof of residential address; beneficial-owner declaration; shareholder register; certified powers of attorney; and written explanation of the ownership and control chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of capital, unusually large initial funding, or capital funded by a third party
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements; audited or management accounts; tax returns where appropriate; sale agreements, dividend records, loan agreements, or investment agreements; capital contribution resolutions; sender-to-recipient relationship evidence; source-of-wealth narrative; and confirmation that funds originate from an account held by the subscriber or a documented financing party.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated company without demonstrated commercial activity or French operating substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan; product catalogue; supplier and logistics contracts; warehouse or fulfilment arrangements; website and customer terms; projected transaction volumes; marketing evidence; director-management profile; office or registered-address agreement; invoices or purchase orders; tax registrations; and a 12-month cash-flow forecast.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Subscription-commerce exposure involving recurring card payments, refunds, chargebacks, consumer complaints, or delivery failures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Payment-flow map; processor agreement; chargeback and refund policy; customer-consent and recurring-payment evidence; delivery and returns procedures; carrier contracts; inventory controls; complaint-management process; fraud-monitoring rules; historic portfolio metrics where available; and reconciliation procedures between orders, settlements, refunds, and bank receipts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned parties, politically exposed persons, adverse media, or unexplained cross-border payment corridors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty register; sanctions and PEP screening records; customer and supplier due-diligence files; country-risk assessment; transaction rationale; end-use and end-customer evidence; beneficial-owner confirmations; compliance officer approval; and enhanced-monitoring plan. Transactions involving sanctioned persons or prohibited jurisdictions must not proceed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared activity and payment flows, including marketplace characteristics, third-party collections, or large cash activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business-model memorandum; contractual allocation of merchant-of-record responsibility; payment-flow diagrams; customer and supplier agreements; sales ledgers; tax and VAT treatment; expected monthly transaction profile; explanation of all third-party payments; and formal prohibition or control of cash-intensive activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete corporate records, expired identification documents, inconsistent registered addresses, or unauthorised account operators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recent corporate registry extract; current articles and resolutions; valid identification documents; address evidence; specimen signatures; director appointment evidence; board or shareholder mandate; authorised-user list; and certified translations where documents are not in an accepted language.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route share capital through a regulated bank or payment institution directly from the subscriber or documented financing entity into the SARL capital-deposit account, using a payment reference such as share capital contribution or capital increase and identifying the company, subscriber, amount, currency, and corporate resolution. The bank should receive the formation documents, draft or executed articles, shareholder and beneficial-owner evidence, source-of-funds documentation, and capital subscription records before releasing funds or issuing the deposit certificate. After registration, transfer or release funds to the operational account only under the bank's procedure. For shareholder loans or intercompany funding, use a written loan agreement, arm's-length terms, repayment schedule, transfer-pricing support where relevant, and source-of-funds evidence. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments within the SEPA area and SWIFT for non-SEPA or foreign-currency payments. Reconcile incoming funds to the general ledger, preserve bank payment messages, and assess any applicable Banque de France statistical reporting, French tax reporting, foreign-account reporting, and direct-investment reporting obligations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro suppliers within the SEPA scheme, subject to bank limits and fraud controls. Use SWIFT customer credit transfer, commonly documented by an MT103 or its ISO 20022 successor equivalent, for non-SEPA or foreign-currency supplier payments. Commercial letters of credit, documentary collections, open-account transfers, and supplier prepayments may be used according to bank policy, underlying contracts, sanctions controls, customs documentation, and trade-finance eligibility. For subscription-box merchandise, retain purchase orders, commercial invoices, packing lists, transport documents, customs declarations, import VAT and duty records, proof of delivery, supplier due diligence, and three-way reconciliation between purchase order, goods receipt, and invoice. Do not split payments to avoid screening or reporting, and ensure payment references accurately identify the invoice and commercial purpose.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorised bank or eligible regulated investment firm, supported by an identified commercial exposure, documented treasury policy, counterparty limits, maturity controls, and accounting treatment.

Non-deliverable forwards may be used for currencies or jurisdictions where delivery is restricted, subject to counterparty authorisation, applicable EU financial-markets rules, suitability and appropriateness requirements, collateral terms, sanctions screening, and a genuine underlying exposure.

Currency swaps and cross-currency swaps may be used for documented recurring or longer-term foreign-currency cash flows, subject to ISDA or equivalent documentation, netting and collateral terms, counterparty credit limits, valuation controls, and regulatory reporting.

Plain-vanilla foreign-exchange options or collars may be used for documented exposure management, subject to premium approval, risk disclosure, valuation, accounting, and prohibition on speculative dealing outside the approved treasury mandate.

Spot foreign-exchange conversions through regulated banks or payment institutions are permissible for operational settlements. Maintain an exposure register, hedge-designation records where applicable, independent valuation, confirmation matching, segregation of dealing and settlement duties, and periodic board-level review.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Minutes of annual shareholders' meeting approving annual accounts and profit appropriation (Décision d'approbation des comptes et affectation du résultat)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; recorded in the mandatory register of shareholders' decisions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end (e.g., 30 June for a 31 December fiscal year); extendable by court order up to an additional 6 months
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to approve within the legal period exposes the manager to civil liability and triggers penalties for late filing of annual accounts; shareholders may seek injunctive relief.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (Dépôt des comptes annuels au RCS) – balance sheet, income statement, notes and management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the Guichet Unique (INPI platform)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of fiscal year-end (e.g., 31 July for a 31 December fiscal year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to EUR 1,500 for natural persons and EUR 7,500 for legal persons for late filing; registration revival fees; the Commercial Court may order compliance under threat of penalty and a forced filing may be published.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner declaration confirmation/update (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs, DBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the Guichet Unique (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Confirmed concurrently with the annual accounts filing; any change in beneficial ownership must be declared within 30 days of the transaction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to EUR 7,500 and 6 months' imprisonment for natural persons; EUR 37,500 fine for legal persons; registry may reject subsequent filings until the DBE is regularized.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Déclaration de résultats n°2065-SD and schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayers, file by the 2nd working day after 1 May of the following year (e.g., 5 May 2025 for FY 2024); for off-calendar fiscal years, within 3 months of year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment increase of 10% on the tax due plus 0.20% monthly interest; return filed after formal notice triggers a 40% assessment penalty (or 80% in cases of willful omission); possible VAT and accounts audits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return for simplified real regime (Déclaration annuelle de TVA n°3517-SD / CA12)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due 3 May following the calendar year for taxpayers under the simplified real regime; monthly filers remain on monthly schemes with no annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of VAT due (10% after formal notice), 0.20% monthly late-payment interest, and possible suspension of VAT credit refunds.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local business franchise tax (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises, CFE) – annual payment and any required change notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP local tax service (Service des Impôts des Entreprises, SIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Return n°1447-C must be filed on creation, cessation or material change of activity; the annual CFE liability is payable by 15 December of the assessment year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment increase of 10% plus 0.20% monthly interest; omitted or false return after notice attracts 40% uplift; enforced collection by the public accountant (comptable public).

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (Commissaire aux Comptes) is mandatory for a SARL if, at the close of a fiscal year, it exceeds two of three thresholds: balance-sheet total greater than EUR 4,000,000; net turnover (excl. VAT) greater than EUR 8,000,000; average workforce greater than 50 employees. Exceeding the thresholds in two consecutive fiscal years is the practical benchmark for continuing obligation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général, PCG) per Code de commerce Articles L.123-12 to L.123-23; IFRS as adopted in the EU is permitted only for consolidated accounts of listed groups; all annual statutory accounts of a SARL must be prepared under French GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The declaration of beneficial owners (DBE) is filed at incorporation and updated within 30 days of any ownership change. Annually, at the time the annual accounts are filed, the company must confirm on the Guichet Unique filing that the beneficial-owner data remains accurate; if a share transfer occurred during the financial year, the update must already have been filed and the confirmation reflects the new ownership structure.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des décisions d'associés (shareholders' decisions and meeting minute book)
Registre des mouvements de titres / cessions de parts (share movements and transfer register)
Registre des procès-verbaux et rapports du commissaire aux comptes (auditor reports and annual general meeting minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 300-600 (annual domiciliation service by a commercial registered-office provider; includes registered address, mail handling and reception)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 6,000-12,000 (typical fee for a compact SARL operating a subscription-box business if the statutory audit threshold is exceeded and a Commissaire aux Comptes is appointed)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard IS rate; 15% reduced rate for qualifying SMEs on first EUR 42,500 of taxable income)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced SME rate of 15% up to EUR 42,500; patent box 50% deduction on qualifying IP income; research credit (CIR) 30%; territorial exemption for foreign permanent establishment profits unless worldwide election; unlimited loss carryforward subject to annual cap of EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of excess taxable income

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (annual corporate income tax return) with liasse fiscale schedules 2052–2059; filed electronically via impots.gouv.fr EFI / EDI-TDFC
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual IS return (quarterly IS prepayments and separate VAT filings apply)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For calendar-year SARL: file by 3 May following the fiscal year-end; for off-calendar fiscal years: within 3 months of the fiscal year-end, adjusted to next working day

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification data: SIREN/SIRET, APE code, registered office, legal form, tax regime
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter French registered office; disclose foreign manager/shareholder addresses and any permanent establishment arrangements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tangible fixed assets, inventories, receivables, cash; subscription box inventory and digital assets
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare French-situs assets only; allocate foreign PE assets and liabilities separately if treaty PE exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report taxable turnover from subscription box sales and ancillary services in statutory currency
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Record cross-border e-commerce sales in EUR; follow FX conversion rules and VAT consequence mapping.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses available for offset against current taxable income; subject to EUR 1M / 50% annual cap
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach substantiation of deficit history; do not include losses from foreign PEs unless treaty allocates losses to France.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: automatic 10% penalty; 40% if filed more than 30 days after formal notice; 80% for concealed or fraudulent activity; late interest 0.20% per month; EUR 150 e-filing non-compliance penalty; potential assessment by DGFiP under Article 1725 LPF.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Domestic WHT on outbound dividends to non-resident companies: 25% under Article 187 CGI; reduced to 0% for EU parent-subsidiary directives; treaty rate generally 0%, 5%, or 15% depending on DTA
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Beneficial owner must deliver a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) to the paying SARL and DGFiP before payment to claim treaty reduction; otherwise, maintain refund claim via Form 5000/non-resident certificate; substance and beneficial ownership must be demonstrated to deny anti-abuse challenges
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory WHT 33.33% under Article 182 B CGI for IP royalties paid abroad; reduced to 0% for associated EU entities under Interest and Royalties Directive; usual DTA rates 0-15%. Interest: generally exempt from French WHT on ordinary commercial loans; 75% WHT applies to interest paid to non-cooperative jurisdictions; treaty rates commonly 0% or 10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File mandatory when group turnover or consolidated assets exceed EUR 400 million; Country-by-Country Reporting at EUR 750 million group revenue; lower thresholds apply when tax administration formally requests
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no offshore-style ESR for onshore SARL; but anti-abuse and GAAR rules (including beneficial ownership doctrine) require real management, staff, and substance for DTA access; shell companies without substance may be recharacterized and lose treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional omission of subscription box revenue, concealed bank accounts, or falsified electronic invoices to DGFiP; structured transactions to hide taxable sales
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalty per Article 1741 CGI: up to 5 years imprisonment and EUR 75,000 fine; civil tax penalties up to 80% plus late interest; seizure and search powers exercised by DGFiP
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Gérant/manager may be personally prosecuted for fraudulent evasion; civil veil-piercing occurs on proof of fictitious or artificial company; travel bans, asset seizure, and disqualification from management.
